VERIFIED: Lekhah Dodi has the opening refrain plus 9 stanzas, and 10 marginal לכה cues (one beside the opening refrain, one after each of stanzas 1–9). The two small notes הש״ץ מנגן בנעימה. and ראשי החרוזים שלמה הלוי. are printed on one line, as two separate items, above the refrain. Stanza 9 prints גַּם בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְצָהֳלָה.

RESIDUAL DEFECT (medium): lekhah_dodi.xml line 44, stanza 8, reads בֶּן־פַּרְצִי. In the enlarged s17 crop, בֶּן ends the line and no maqaf is visible, while other line-final maqafs in this volume are clearly printed (97:9 עַל־כָּל־, 29:2 בְּהַדְרַת־, 95:3 עַל־). The enlarged independent reading itself warned that customary pointing may have filled gaps in this poem. The adjudication does not address this word. findings.rule: Words joined by maqaf are one unit; nothing may be placed between them
findings.evidence: עַל־כָּל־ <tei:pb .../>אֱלֹהִים: has whitespace after the maqaf. psalm_29.xml line 41 has the same pattern: בְּהַדְרַת־ <tei:pb/>קֹדֶשׁ. A renderer may split the maqaf unit.
findings.required_fix: Remove the space so the pb sits directly between the maqaf and the next word (…כָּל־<tei:pb/>אֱלֹהִים), in both files.

findings.rule: Exact same-unit terminators, chapter/verse milestones, abbr/expan, rend, citation notes
findings.evidence: All eight chapters open with a chapter milestone (n and corresp) and verse milestones, and close with a bare verse terminator followed by a bare chapter terminator. Each paragraph follows the printed paragraph, independent of the verse milestones. Role labels are type=description notes with role URNs and tei:choice abbr/expan (ח׳/חזן, ק׳/קהל, קו״ח/קהל וחזן), so the reader can choose abbreviated or expanded. No @rend appears on any rubric. The citations are bare Hebrew numerals in standOff notes, with no added parentheses. Eruv prayer-parts and the poem's refrain/stanza sequences are explicitly terminated. All declare/endDeclare and conditional/endConditional pairs in the expanded index match: checked by static reading.

findings: STATIC ORDER (verified by reading index.xml): entering the synagogue → Erev RH Minchah (gated Elul 29, not Shabbat or Yom Tov) → eruv (Elul 29 plus the derived eruv-tavshilin setting) → festival lights (RH day 1, Maariv; weekday branch shabbat=false → bare hadlaqat_ner_yom_tov; Shabbat branch → bare hadlaqat_ner_yom_tov/shabbat) → Kabbalat Shabbat (shabbat plus Maariv) → morning. Every declaration and condition before the morning section closes before line 655 (endDeclare/endConditional at lines 351/353, 449/451, 651/653).

Kabbalat sequence: Psalms 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 29, then Lekhah Dodi, then Psalms 92 and 93, then a Mourner's Kaddish gated on minyan plus mourners present. This matches the printed order on s13–s17, including the printed קדיש יתום direction. The kaddish/yatom URN is in the registry (prayer.jsonl line 380).

Lekhah Dodi expansion: opening refrain, opening response, then stanza n followed by response n for n = 1–9. That is 11 transclusions of the bare poem:lekhah_dodi/refrain URN and 9 unique stanza URNs. The source keeps one refrain occurrence and 10 literal cues. The opening response depends on the human clarification (the opening לכה cue means a repeat), recorded in preparations_kabbalat_resolutions.json. It is not visible as a direction in the scan beyond the marginal cue.

The Shabbat lights branch resolves only to the new Birnbaum extraction, which pins its own parent with @hasiddur_hashalem-birnbaum-1949-he. No English is supplied for the combined blessing, which matches the expanded sourceDesc note at line 39. The weekday branch resolves to the preferred Marmorstein witness. Whether each bare URN resolves to the intended project is static inference only, from project priorities I did not inspect.

RITUAL-POLICY UNCERTAINTY (open; scope depends on a pending user clarification): when RH day 1 falls on Shabbat, many Ashkenazi communities, the German rite among them, begin Kabbalat Shabbat at Psalm 92 and omit Psalms 95–99, 29 and Lekhah Dodi. Birnbaum prints such an omission direction; these leaves print none. The current encoding keeps the full printed sequence on the explicit assumption the user stated, and correctly does not carry over Birnbaum's rule. Stanza 9 printing בְּשִׂמְחָה (a wording some editions keep for Yom Tov) is at most weak evidence and does not settle the question. Until the user answers, flag this section as an editorial assumption.

The Kabbalat gate (line 454) does not test rosh-hashana, unlike the lights gate. This is harmless in this volume, but the section would also show on any Shabbat-Maariv date if the expanded book were compiled with non-RH settings.

Static inference only: that 1 Tishrei Maariv on a Friday evening derives shabbat=true and rosh-hashana=1, that eruv-tavshilin derives true on Elul 29 only when RH falls on Thursday–Friday, and that opensiddur:service-context/mourners-present and opensiddur:quorum/minyan are registered features. None of this was checked against features.yaml or the calendar code.
